newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says peace talks with rebels postponed.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says peace talks with rebels postponed.

text.p: Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohammad Taha said peace talks between the Khartoum government and the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) had been postponed.
The talks were scheduled for August 19 in Nairobi.

Sudanese state television quoted Taha as saying on Saturday that the Kenyan Foreign Ministry informed his ministry that the talks arranged by the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) had been put off indefinitely.
IGAD is made up of a group of African countries working on an initiative to end the civil war in Sudan, being fought mostly in the south.
The group comprises Kenya, Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Uganda, Somalia and Djibouti.
"The Kenyan government did not explain the circumstances surrounding the postponement," Taha said.
The SPLA, under leader John Garang, has been behind most of the fighting against the Sudanese government.
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir called for a ceasefire in the 14-year war with the SPLA during a visit to South Africa on Tuesday.

The war in Sudan, Africa's largest country, has pitted Christian and animist rebels in the south against the Moslem and Arabised north. The rebels want greater autonomy or independence from the north.
